request.what: Hardware Wallet Maintenance 2026 for production maintenance of Cardano hardware-wallet support, including Ledger and Trezor compatibility updates, supporting interoperability libraries and cardano-hw-cli, developer support, externally maintained integration paths where hardware-wallet flows intersect, and vendor-required product or security audits.

claims.claim: The proposal requests 1,310,960 ada, consisting of 1,272,777 ada for Cardano Hardware Wallet Maintenance & Compatibility Assurance and 38,183 ada for the Intersect Budget Administration fee.

The work is framed as continuity for an already-proven Cardano access layer rather than a new wallet product, with scope limited to compatibility, security, libraries, tooling, release support, and vendor-required audit work.

The proposer states that continuous maintenance is needed because Cardano protocol evolution, Ledger and Trezor release cycles, and wallet and dApp integration demand create compatibility risk for hardware-wallet users and integrators.

The proposal says the work will preserve secure signing, avoid broken builder integrations, prevent protocol and vendor changes from stranding hardware-wallet users, and support newer utility layers that rely on maintained hardware-wallet paths.

The proposal asserts alignment with Cardano strategic Pillar 1 for security, reliability, and interoperability, and secondary alignment with Pillar 2 for adoption, UX, enterprise-grade security, developer experience, and compatibility with common tooling.

The proposal states it achieved the required 67% support threshold during the 2026 Intersect Budget Process Hydra Voting phase and was advanced for on-chain submission under the approved Budget Process Framework.
The proposer states that the requested amount does not, at submission, breach the applicable 350M ada Net Change Limit covering Epoch 613 to Epoch 713, either alone or in aggregate.

Intersect plans to administer funds through a 2026 Treasury Reserve Smart Contract and one Project-Specific Smart Contract, with listed stake and payment addresses, on-chain logic, and dashboard-based community auditability.

The document says oversight will involve five Intersect admins, three Intersect leadership roles, and six external entities with specified multi-party authorization thresholds for funding, disbursement, pause/resume, sweep, and reorganize actions.

The proposal discloses prior related treasury or Catalyst funding links for hardware wallet maintenance, Ledger app rewrite, Plutus enhancement, Ledger Live integration, message signing, security, token extension, and CTF-related work.

summary: The document requests 1,310,960 ada for 2026 hardware-wallet maintenance administered by Intersect through treasury smart contracts, with asserted technical continuity benefits, disclosed budget lines, governance-process references, NCL compliance claims, and oversight details, but it does not provide a full feasibility, risk, alternatives, failure-mode, or detailed budget justification in the anchor text.
